hints.title: Rate-Limited Invocations with Trailing Execution
hints.text: Throttling ensures that a target function is triggered at most once per time window, executing immediately on the leading edge and postponing the most recent call to the trailing edge.

hints.title: Timer Flag and Trailing Arguments Staging
hints.text: If no timer is active, execute immediately and set a cooldown timer. If calls arrive during cooldown, save the latest arguments. When cooldown expires, execute with saved arguments if present.

hints.title: Throttle Blueprint
hints.text: Variables: timeoutId = null, nextArgs = null. In wrapper(...args): if timeoutId is null, execute fn(...args) and schedule helper after delay t; otherwise store latest arguments in nextArgs. helper(): if nextArgs exists, invoke fn(...nextArgs), clear nextArgs, and reschedule helper; else reset timeoutId to null.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Timer scheduling and argument swapping execute in constant time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simple debouncing postpones execution indefinitely while bursts continue, whereas throttling guarantees periodic execution.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Retaining only the latest arguments avoids memory queues for intermediate suppressed invocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling both leading execution and trailing execution with the most recent argument payload.
